title: Perturbed quantum billiards on the hyperbolic plane
abstract: We study the emergence of generic quantum chaos from an arithmetic billiard in the hyperbolic plane. Starting from an arithmetic triangle, we introduce small area-preserving geometric perturbations and compute long consecutive sequences of eigenvalues and eigenstates. The spectral statistics show a perturbation-dependent crossover from Poisson-like arithmetic behaviour to the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (GOE), with the crossover scale moving to higher wavenumbers as the perturbation decreases. To characterize the nearest-neighbour spacing distribution, we compare the data with Brody and generalized-gamma fits. The generalized-gamma form is used only as a two-parameter diagnostic, allowing the small- and intermediate-spacing structure to vary independently from the large-spacing tail, rather than as a universal crossover law. For the weakest perturbation, we also compare the data with an effective block-GOE model, which diagnoses residual block-like structure deep into the computed spectral range. We complement the spectral analysis with Poincaré-Husimi representations of the eigenstates and quantify phase-space localization using an entropy-based measure. Its distribution is well described by Beta distributions whose width decays as a power law in the wavenumber. Before the spectral crossover, the localization statistics retain memory of the near-arithmetic regime. After the GOE regime is reached, the localization-fluctuation widths collapse onto a common decay law, sigma(Beta) ~ k^{-eta}, with eta approximately 0.37--0.38. These results provide a combined spectral and eigenfunction-level picture of the arithmetic-to-GOE crossover in hyperbolic quantum billiards.
summary: This work analyzes the emergence of quantum chaos in hyperbolic billiards by perturbing an initially arithmetic system. The authors show a clear crossover from Poisson statistics to GOE behavior in both eigenvalue spacing and eigenfunction localization measures. This provides a comprehensive, combined spectral and wave-function view of how symmetries break down into generic chaotic dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates how generic quantum chaos emerges from an arithmetic billiard defined on the hyperbolic plane when subjected to small geometric perturbations.
main_result: Both spectral statistics and eigenfunction localization measures exhibit a measurable crossover from Poisson-like (arithmetic) behavior towards Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE) statistics, characterized by a common power-law decay in their respective widths.
method: The analysis combines spectral theory (analyzing nearest-neighbor spacing distributions) with eigenfunction analysis using Poincaré–Husimi representations and entropy measures on the boundary phase space.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum billiard defined by the Laplace–Beltrami operator on a hyperbolic domain, specifically starting from an arithmetic triangle (Schmit triangle) in the Poincaré disk model. Small area-preserving perturbations are introduced to break the initial arithmetic symmetries.
key_observables: Nearest-neighbor spacing distribution ($P(s)$), spectral rigidity, localization entropy width ($\sigma_{	ext{Beta}}$), and the crossover scale of these statistics.
important_parameters: The perturbation strength ($\epsilon$), which controls the transition from Poisson to GOE behavior; the wavenumber ($k$).
main_assumptions: The generalized-gamma fit is used only as a diagnostic tool, not as a universal law. The analysis relies on comparing results across different levels of perturbation strength.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the hyperbolic tessellation and show convergence behavior related to computational parameters like points-per-wavelength; tables list specific perturbation values ($\epsilon$) and resulting changes in arclength ($L$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical system (hyperbolic billiard) and its initial arithmetic state, through applying spectral analysis techniques (diagnostics for crossover), to complementing this with eigenfunction localization studies that confirm the same transition mechanism.
why_interesting: It provides a detailed, quantitative picture of quantum chaos transitions in non-Euclidean geometries, linking number theory (arithmetic billiards) directly to universal random matrix theory predictions (GOE).

figures.caption: FIG. 1 Finite-depth reflection tessellation of the Schmit triangle in the Poincar´e disk (1). The red triangle de- notes the fundamental billiard domain, whose angles are π/8, π/2, and π/3. Since each angle is an integer submul- tiple of π, repeated reflections in the three geodesic sides generate a hyperbolic triangle group and tile the hyper- bolic plane without gaps or overlaps. The black curves show a finite subset of this infinite tessellation; the accu- mulation of smaller copies near the unit circle reflects the compression of hyperbolic distance in the Poincar´e disk model.

FIG. 2 Example classical trajectory in Schmit’s hyper- bolic triangle. The black curve shows the billiard bound- ary in the Poincar´e disk model, and the red arcs show several specular reflections of a geodesic trajectory. The two sides emanating from the origin are radial geodesics, while the third side is a circular arc orthogonal to the unit disk boundary.
